official_source_terms: California Department of Public Health West Nile virus
likely_reporting_agencies: California Department of Public Health (CDPH) – Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS)
CDC Division of Vector-Borne Diseases (DVBD)
County/Local Health Departments (e.g., Los Angeles County DPH, Sacramento County DPH, Kern County DPH, Fresno County DPH)

CDC ArboNET national surveillance system

validation_source_categories: County-level health department press releases or dashboards
count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports cumulative year-to-date human cases; subtract prior period totals if only August 2024 incident counts are needed
ArboNET data may lag by 1–2 weeks from actual reporting date
Neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts should be recorded separately if available, then summed for cases_unspecified if not stratified
Deaths are often underreported in real-time surveillance; cross-check with MMWR annual summaries
Probable cases in WNV context = IgM positive without confirmatory PRNT; confirmed = PRNT or PCR confirmed
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often include animal/vector data alongside human data — extract human cases only
Cumulative vs. incident counts: CDPH reports are often cumulative year-to-date; isolate August 2024 period carefully
Confirmed vs. probable: CDPH and ArboNET distinguish confirmed (lab-confirmed) from probable (clinical + epidemiological link); capture both separately
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive: case counts are often stratified; aggregate or record separately per schema
'Cases' may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird counts in some county reports — verify human case context
County-level reports may use different reporting dates than state-level aggregates — note discrepancies

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) weekly or monthly WNV human surveillance reports for California covering August 2024, extracting confirmed, probable, and suspected human case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations by county.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH VBDS is the primary authoritative source for human WNV case surveillance in California, publishing weekly summaries with county-level breakdowns that directly map to target fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county-level health department (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside) WNV human case reports or press releases published during or covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County health departments often publish local WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than the state, enabling locality-level record extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET state-level WNV human case data for California for 2024, specifically any tabular or dashboard data covering the August 2024 reporting window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case and death counts that can serve as a primary or corroborating collection source.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured or summary sources (e.g., CDC WONDER, ProMED, PAHO situation reports) reporting California WNV human case totals for 2024 to cross-validate collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators and international health organization reports provide held-back validation data to detect count discrepancies or misclassification in collected records.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV seasonality, high-risk counties, and case definitions provide context for interpreting August 2024 surveillance data. count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports cumulative year-to-date human cases; subtract prior period totals if only August 2024 incident counts are needed
ArboNET data may lag by 1–2 weeks from actual reporting date
Neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts should be recorded separately if available, then summed for cases_unspecified if not stratified

Probable cases in WNV context = IgM positive without confirmatory PRNT; confirmed = PRNT or PCR confirmed
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often include animal/vector data alongside human data — extract human cases only
Cumulative vs. incident counts: CDPH reports are often cumulative year-to-date; isolate August 2024 period carefully
Confirmed vs. probable: CDPH and ArboNET distinguish confirmed (lab-confirmed) from probable (clinical + epidemiological link); capture both separately
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive: case counts are often stratified; aggregate or record separately per schema
'Cases' may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird counts in some county reports — verify human case context
County-level reports may use different reporting dates than state-level aggregates — note discrepancies

core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths

core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

Neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts should be recorded separately if available, then summed for cases_unspecified if not stratified

Probable cases in WNV context = IgM positive without confirmatory PRNT; confirmed = PRNT or PCR confirmed
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often include animal/vector data alongside human data — extract human cases only
Cumulative vs. incident counts: CDPH reports are often cumulative year-to-date; isolate August 2024 period carefully
Confirmed vs. probable: CDPH and ArboNET distinguish confirmed (lab-confirmed) from probable (clinical + epidemiological link); capture both separately
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive: case counts are often stratified; aggregate or record separately per schema
'Cases' may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird counts in some county reports — verify human case context
County-level reports may use different reporting dates than state-level aggregates — note discrepancies

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) publishes weekly WNV human surveillance summaries with county-level confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. County health departments (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside, San Bernardino, Orange) publish local WNV human case alerts and press releases. These are the highest-priority primary collection sources for the August 2024 California window.

CDC ArboNET publishes structured state-level WNV human case and death data. California open data portals (data.ca.gov) and CDPH open data may expose machine-readable WNV surveillance datasets filterable by county and date, enabling programmatic validation of narrative report extractions.

PAHO and WHO may publish situation reports or epidemiological updates referencing US WNV human case data including California. ProMED-mail archives WNV outbreak alerts that may cite CDPH or CDC data for California August 2024.

Reputable California news outlets (Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Outbreak News Today) may report WNV human case counts citing CDPH or county health department data for August 2024, providing early signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV seasonality, high-risk counties, and case definitions provide context for interpreting August 2024 surveillance data. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific case counts given publication lag, but useful for case definition and count semantics context.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports cumulative year-to-date human cases; subtract prior period totals if only August 2024 incident counts are needed

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) publishes weekly WNV human surveillance summaries with county-level confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. County health departments (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside, San Bernardino, Orange) publish local WNV human case alerts and press releases. These are the highest-priority primary collection sources for the August 2024 California window.

CDC ArboNET publishes structured state-level WNV human case and death data. California open data portals (data.ca.gov) and CDPH open data may expose machine-readable WNV surveillance datasets filterable by county and date, enabling programmatic validation of narrative report extractions.

PAHO and WHO may publish situation reports or epidemiological updates referencing US WNV human case data including California. ProMED-mail archives WNV outbreak alerts that may cite CDPH or CDC data for California August 2024.

Reputable California news outlets (Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Outbreak News Today) may report WNV human case counts citing CDPH or county health department data for August 2024, providing early signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV seasonality, high-risk counties, and case definitions provide context for interpreting August 2024 surveillance data. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific case counts given publication lag, but useful for case definition and count semantics context.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports cumulative year-to-date human cases; subtract prior period totals if only August 2024 incident counts are needed

Neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts should be recorded separately if available, then summed for cases_unspecified if not stratified

Probable cases in WNV context = IgM positive without confirmatory PRNT; confirmed = PRNT or PCR confirmed
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often include animal/vector data alongside human data — extract human cases only
Cumulative vs. incident counts: CDPH reports are often cumulative year-to-date; isolate August 2024 period carefully
Confirmed vs. probable: CDPH and ArboNET distinguish confirmed (lab-confirmed) from probable (clinical + epidemiological link); capture both separately
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive: case counts are often stratified; aggregate or record separately per schema
'Cases' may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird counts in some county reports — verify human case context
County-level reports may use different reporting dates than state-level aggregates — note discrepancies

Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive: case counts are often stratified; aggregate or record separately per schema

Reputable California news outlets (Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Outbreak News Today) may report WNV human case counts citing CDPH or county health department data for August 2024, providing early signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV seasonality, high-risk counties, and case definitions provide context for interpreting August 2024 surveillance data. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific case counts given publication lag, but useful for case definition and count semantics context.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) weekly or monthly WNV human surveillance reports for California covering August 2024, extracting confirmed, probable, and suspected human case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations by county.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH VBDS is the primary authoritative source for human WNV case surveillance in California, publishing weekly summaries with county-level breakdowns that directly map to target fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county-level health department (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside) WNV human case reports or press releases published during or covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County health departments often publish local WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than the state, enabling locality-level record extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET state-level WNV human case data for California for 2024, specifically any tabular or dashboard data covering the August 2024 reporting window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case and death counts that can serve as a primary or corroborating collection source.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured or summary sources (e.g., CDC WONDER, ProMED, PAHO situation reports) reporting California WNV human case totals for 2024 to cross-validate collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators and international health organization reports provide held-back validation data to detect count discrepancies or misclassification in collected records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California WNV open data portal datasets or structured surveillance exports (e.g., data.ca.gov, CDPH open data) with human case counts filterable by date and county for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured database exports allow programmatic cross-validation of case counts against narrative reports, reducing manual extraction error.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile neuroinvasive disease (WNND) and West Nile fever (WNF) to clarify confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classification used in California 2024 surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine how counts are classified across confirmed, probable, and suspected fields; misapplication leads to systematic extraction errors.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV seasonality, transmission patterns, and high-risk counties to contextualize August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Epidemiological context helps interpret whether August 2024 counts are anomalous, cumulative, or newly reported, and supports correct assignment of statistical_count_type.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report only animal (equine, avian), mosquito pool, or sentinel chicken WNV positivity without human case data, or that aggregate California into multi-state or national totals without subnational breakdown.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources reporting only non-human WNV or national aggregates without California-specific human counts must be excluded or quarantined per task acceptance contract exclusion rules.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) publishes weekly WNV human surveillance summaries with county-level confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. County health departments (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside, San Bernardino, Orange) publish local WNV human case alerts and press releases. These are the highest-priority primary collection sources for the August 2024 California window.

CDC ArboNET publishes structured state-level WNV human case and death data. California open data portals (data.ca.gov) and CDPH open data may expose machine-readable WNV surveillance datasets filterable by county and date, enabling programmatic validation of narrative report extractions.

PAHO and WHO may publish situation reports or epidemiological updates referencing US WNV human case data including California. ProMED-mail archives WNV outbreak alerts that may cite CDPH or CDC data for California August 2024.

Reputable California news outlets (Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Outbreak News Today) may report WNV human case counts citing CDPH or county health department data for August 2024, providing early signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV seasonality, high-risk counties, and case definitions provide context for interpreting August 2024 surveillance data. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific case counts given publication lag, but useful for case definition and count semantics context.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) weekly or monthly WNV human surveillance reports for California covering August 2024, extracting confirmed, probable, and suspected human case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations by county.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH VBDS is the primary authoritative source for human WNV case surveillance in California, publishing weekly summaries with county-level breakdowns that directly map to target fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county-level health department (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside) WNV human case reports or press releases published during or covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County health departments often publish local WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than the state, enabling locality-level record extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET state-level WNV human case data for California for 2024, specifically any tabular or dashboard data covering the August 2024 reporting window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case and death counts that can serve as a primary or corroborating collection source.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured or summary sources (e.g., CDC WONDER, ProMED, PAHO situation reports) reporting California WNV human case totals for 2024 to cross-validate collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators and international health organization reports provide held-back validation data to detect count discrepancies or misclassification in collected records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California WNV open data portal datasets or structured surveillance exports (e.g., data.ca.gov, CDPH open data) with human case counts filterable by date and county for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured database exports allow programmatic cross-validation of case counts against narrative reports, reducing manual extraction error.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile neuroinvasive disease (WNND) and West Nile fever (WNF) to clarify confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classification used in California 2024 surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine how counts are classified across confirmed, probable, and suspected fields; misapplication leads to systematic extraction errors.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV seasonality, transmission patterns, and high-risk counties to contextualize August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Epidemiological context helps interpret whether August 2024 counts are anomalous, cumulative, or newly reported, and supports correct assignment of statistical_count_type.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report only animal (equine, avian), mosquito pool, or sentinel chicken WNV positivity without human case data, or that aggregate California into multi-state or national totals without subnational breakdown.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources reporting only non-human WNV or national aggregates without California-specific human counts must be excluded or quarantined per task acceptance contract exclusion rules.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) publishes weekly WNV human surveillance summaries with county-level confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. County health departments (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside, San Bernardino, Orange) publish local WNV human case alerts and press releases. These are the highest-priority primary collection sources for the August 2024 California window.

CDC ArboNET publishes structured state-level WNV human case and death data. California open data portals (data.ca.gov) and CDPH open data may expose machine-readable WNV surveillance datasets filterable by county and date, enabling programmatic validation of narrative report extractions.

PAHO and WHO may publish situation reports or epidemiological updates referencing US WNV human case data including California. ProMED-mail archives WNV outbreak alerts that may cite CDPH or CDC data for California August 2024.

Reputable California news outlets (Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Outbreak News Today) may report WNV human case counts citing CDPH or county health department data for August 2024, providing early signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV seasonality, high-risk counties, and case definitions provide context for interpreting August 2024 surveillance data. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific case counts given publication lag, but useful for case definition and count semantics context.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) weekly or monthly WNV human surveillance reports for California covering August 2024, extracting confirmed, probable, and suspected human case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations by county.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH VBDS is the primary authoritative source for human WNV case surveillance in California, publishing weekly summaries with county-level breakdowns that directly map to target fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county-level health department (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside) WNV human case reports or press releases published during or covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County health departments often publish local WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than the state, enabling locality-level record extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET state-level WNV human case data for California for 2024, specifically any tabular or dashboard data covering the August 2024 reporting window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case and death counts that can serve as a primary or corroborating collection source.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured or summary sources (e.g., CDC WONDER, ProMED, PAHO situation reports) reporting California WNV human case totals for 2024 to cross-validate collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators and international health organization reports provide held-back validation data to detect count discrepancies or misclassification in collected records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California WNV open data portal datasets or structured surveillance exports (e.g., data.ca.gov, CDPH open data) with human case counts filterable by date and county for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured database exports allow programmatic cross-validation of case counts against narrative reports, reducing manual extraction error.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile neuroinvasive disease (WNND) and West Nile fever (WNF) to clarify confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classification used in California 2024 surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine how counts are classified across confirmed, probable, and suspected fields; misapplication leads to systematic extraction errors.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV seasonality, transmission patterns, and high-risk counties to contextualize August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Epidemiological context helps interpret whether August 2024 counts are anomalous, cumulative, or newly reported, and supports correct assignment of statistical_count_type.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report only animal (equine, avian), mosquito pool, or sentinel chicken WNV positivity without human case data, or that aggregate California into multi-state or national totals without subnational breakdown.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources reporting only non-human WNV or national aggregates without California-specific human counts must be excluded or quarantined per task acceptance contract exclusion rules.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) publishes weekly WNV human surveillance summaries with county-level confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports cumulative year-to-date human cases; subtract prior period totals if only August 2024 incident counts are needed
ArboNET data may lag by 1–2 weeks from actual reporting date
Neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts should be recorded separately if available, then summed for cases_unspecified if not stratified
Deaths are often underreported in real-time surveillance; cross-check with MMWR annual summaries
Probable cases in WNV context = IgM positive without confirmatory PRNT; confirmed = PRNT or PCR confirmed
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often include animal/vector data alongside human data — extract human cases only
Cumulative vs. incident counts: CDPH reports are often cumulative year-to-date; isolate August 2024 period carefully
Confirmed vs. probable: CDPH and ArboNET distinguish confirmed (lab-confirmed) from probable (clinical + epidemiological link); capture both separately
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive: case counts are often stratified; aggregate or record separately per schema
'Cases' may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird counts in some county reports — verify human case context
County-level reports may use different reporting dates than state-level aggregates — note discrepancies

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports cumulative year-to-date human cases; subtract prior period totals if only August 2024 incident counts are needed
ArboNET data may lag by 1–2 weeks from actual reporting date
Neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts should be recorded separately if available, then summed for cases_unspecified if not stratified
Deaths are often underreported in real-time surveillance; cross-check with MMWR annual summaries
Probable cases in WNV context = IgM positive without confirmatory PRNT; confirmed = PRNT or PCR confirmed
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often include animal/vector data alongside human data — extract human cases only
Cumulative vs. incident counts: CDPH reports are often cumulative year-to-date; isolate August 2024 period carefully
Confirmed vs. probable: CDPH and ArboNET distinguish confirmed (lab-confirmed) from probable (clinical + epidemiological link); capture both separately
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive: case counts are often stratified; aggregate or record separately per schema
'Cases' may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird counts in some county reports — verify human case context
County-level reports may use different reporting dates than state-level aggregates — note discrepancies

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) weekly or monthly WNV human surveillance reports for California covering August 2024, extracting confirmed, probable, and suspected human case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations by county.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH VBDS is the primary authoritative source for human WNV case surveillance in California, publishing weekly summaries with county-level breakdowns that directly map to target fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county-level health department (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside) WNV human case reports or press releases published during or covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County health departments often publish local WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than the state, enabling locality-level record extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET state-level WNV human case data for California for 2024, specifically any tabular or dashboard data covering the August 2024 reporting window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case and death counts that can serve as a primary or corroborating collection source.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured or summary sources (e.g., CDC WONDER, ProMED, PAHO situation reports) reporting California WNV human case totals for 2024 to cross-validate collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators and international health organization reports provide held-back validation data to detect count discrepancies or misclassification in collected records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California WNV open data portal datasets or structured surveillance exports (e.g., data.ca.gov, CDPH open data) with human case counts filterable by date and county for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured database exports allow programmatic cross-validation of case counts against narrative reports, reducing manual extraction error.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile neuroinvasive disease (WNND) and West Nile fever (WNF) to clarify confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classification used in California 2024 surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine how counts are classified across confirmed, probable, and suspected fields; misapplication leads to systematic extraction errors.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV seasonality, transmission patterns, and high-risk counties to contextualize August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Epidemiological context helps interpret whether August 2024 counts are anomalous, cumulative, or newly reported, and supports correct assignment of statistical_count_type.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report only animal (equine, avian), mosquito pool, or sentinel chicken WNV positivity without human case data, or that aggregate California into multi-state or national totals without subnational breakdown.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources reporting only non-human WNV or national aggregates without California-specific human counts must be excluded or quarantined per task acceptance contract exclusion rules.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) publishes weekly WNV human surveillance summaries with county-level confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. County health departments (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside, San Bernardino, Orange) publish local WNV human case alerts and press releases. These are the highest-priority primary collection sources for the August 2024 California window.

CDC ArboNET publishes structured state-level WNV human case and death data. California open data portals (data.ca.gov) and CDPH open data may expose machine-readable WNV surveillance datasets filterable by county and date, enabling programmatic validation of narrative report extractions.

PAHO and WHO may publish situation reports or epidemiological updates referencing US WNV human case data including California. ProMED-mail archives WNV outbreak alerts that may cite CDPH or CDC data for California August 2024.

Reputable California news outlets (Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Outbreak News Today) may report WNV human case counts citing CDPH or county health department data for August 2024, providing early signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV seasonality, high-risk counties, and case definitions provide context for interpreting August 2024 surveillance data. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific case counts given publication lag, but useful for case definition and count semantics context.

'Neuroinvasive' is the standard CDC/CDPH classification term for severe WNV disease and will help surface case-classification data. Avoids over-quoted exact phrases that may not match real page text.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH press release, county health department advisory, or westnile.ca.gov summary referencing August 2024 case counts
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Source attributed to CDPH, a California county public health department, or official state surveillance program

query_batch.query: CDC ArboNET West Nile virus 2024 California cases deaths statistics
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system that aggregates state-reported WNV data including California. It publishes annual and weekly case statistics by state, including confirmed/probable cases, neuroinvasive disease, and deaths. This provides a cross-validation source independent of CDPH and may include August 2024 cumulative figures.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC ArboNET weekly or annual WNV statistics table for 2024 with California state row
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: CDC.gov domain; data labeled as ArboNET surveillance system output

query_batch.query: "West Nile virus" California 2024 cases deaths August outbreak health department
query_batch.query_rationale: News articles published in August 2024 frequently cite official CDPH or county health department figures and can surface specific case counts, deaths, and locality data that corroborate or supplement official reports. This query uses natural language terms without over-quoted phrases to maximize recall across news outlets covering the California WNV season peak.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: News article from California regional or statewide outlet (e.g., LA Times, Sacramento Bee, SF Chronicle) citing CDPH or county health figures for August 2024 WNV cases
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Article cites CDPH, county health officer, or westnile.ca.gov as data source; published between 2024-08-01 and 2024-09-15

California public health reporting for West Nile virus is conducted exclusively in English by state and county agencies. No Spanish-language or other localized sources are expected to provide primary surveillance data for this task. No localization adjustments are needed.

Medium trust: News articles — useful for surfacing specific figures and dates but must be verified against official sources; treat as collection_support only

[en Español](spanish.php)

West Nile virus (WNV) is a mosquito-borne virus that causes disease in humans, horses, and birds. count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports cumulative year-to-date human cases; subtract prior period totals if only August 2024 incident counts are needed
ArboNET data may lag by 1–2 weeks from actual reporting date
Neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts should be recorded separately if available, then summed for cases_unspecified if not stratified
Deaths are often underreported in real-time surveillance; cross-check with MMWR annual summaries
Probable cases in WNV context = IgM positive without confirmatory PRNT; confirmed = PRNT or PCR confirmed
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often include animal/vector data alongside human data — extract human cases only
Cumulative vs. incident counts: CDPH reports are often cumulative year-to-date; isolate August 2024 period carefully
Confirmed vs. probable: CDPH and ArboNET distinguish confirmed (lab-confirmed) from probable (clinical + epidemiological link); capture both separately
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive: case counts are often stratified; aggregate or record separately per schema
'Cases' may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird counts in some county reports — verify human case context
County-level reports may use different reporting dates than state-level aggregates — note discrepancies

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports cumulative year-to-date human cases; subtract prior period totals if only August 2024 incident counts are needed
ArboNET data may lag by 1–2 weeks from actual reporting date
Neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts should be recorded separately if available, then summed for cases_unspecified if not stratified
Deaths are often underreported in real-time surveillance; cross-check with MMWR annual summaries
Probable cases in WNV context = IgM positive without confirmatory PRNT; confirmed = PRNT or PCR confirmed
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often include animal/vector data alongside human data — extract human cases only
Cumulative vs. incident counts: CDPH reports are often cumulative year-to-date; isolate August 2024 period carefully
Confirmed vs. probable: CDPH and ArboNET distinguish confirmed (lab-confirmed) from probable (clinical + epidemiological link); capture both separately
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive: case counts are often stratified; aggregate or record separately per schema
'Cases' may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird counts in some county reports — verify human case context
County-level reports may use different reporting dates than state-level aggregates — note discrepancies

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) weekly or monthly WNV human surveillance reports for California covering August 2024, extracting confirmed, probable, and suspected human case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations by county.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH VBDS is the primary authoritative source for human WNV case surveillance in California, publishing weekly summaries with county-level breakdowns that directly map to target fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county-level health department (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside) WNV human case reports or press releases published during or covering August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County health departments often publish local WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than the state, enabling locality-level record extraction.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET state-level WNV human case data for California for 2024, specifically any tabular or dashboard data covering the August 2024 reporting window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case and death counts that can serve as a primary or corroborating collection source.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured or summary sources (e.g., CDC WONDER, ProMED, PAHO situation reports) reporting California WNV human case totals for 2024 to cross-validate collected records.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators and international health organization reports provide held-back validation data to detect count discrepancies or misclassification in collected records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California WNV open data portal datasets or structured surveillance exports (e.g., data.ca.gov, CDPH open data) with human case counts filterable by date and county for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured database exports allow programmatic cross-validation of case counts against narrative reports, reducing manual extraction error.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definition documents for West Nile neuroinvasive disease (WNND) and West Nile fever (WNF) to clarify confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected classification used in California 2024 surveillance.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Case definitions determine how counts are classified across confirmed, probable, and suspected fields; misapplication leads to systematic extraction errors.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV seasonality, transmission patterns, and high-risk counties to contextualize August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Epidemiological context helps interpret whether August 2024 counts are anomalous, cumulative, or newly reported, and supports correct assignment of statistical_count_type.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report only animal (equine, avian), mosquito pool, or sentinel chicken WNV positivity without human case data, or that aggregate California into multi-state or national totals without subnational breakdown.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources reporting only non-human WNV or national aggregates without California-specific human counts must be excluded or quarantined per task acceptance contract exclusion rules.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) publishes weekly WNV human surveillance summaries with county-level confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. County health departments (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside, San Bernardino, Orange) publish local WNV human case alerts and press releases. These are the highest-priority primary collection sources for the August 2024 California window.

CDC ArboNET publishes structured state-level WNV human case and death data. California open data portals (data.ca.gov) and CDPH open data may expose machine-readable WNV surveillance datasets filterable by county and date, enabling programmatic validation of narrative report extractions.

PAHO and WHO may publish situation reports or epidemiological updates referencing US WNV human case data including California. ProMED-mail archives WNV outbreak alerts that may cite CDPH or CDC data for California August 2024.

Reputable California news outlets (Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Outbreak News Today) may report WNV human case counts citing CDPH or county health department data for August 2024, providing early signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV seasonality, high-risk counties, and case definitions provide context for interpreting August 2024 surveillance data. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific case counts given publication lag, but useful for case definition and count semantics context.

iterative_search_queries.query: West Nile virus California 2024 human cases deaths weekly report site:westnile.ca.gov OR site:cdph.ca.gov
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: The California West Nile Virus website (westnile.ca.gov) and CDPH (cdph.ca.gov) are the primary authoritative sources for weekly WNV human surveillance summaries in California. These pages publish cumulative and weekly case counts, deaths, neuroinvasive disease counts, and county breakdowns. Targeting these domains directly maximizes the chance of retrieving the August 2024 weekly reports.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH or westnile.ca.gov weekly WNV surveillance summary page with tabular case counts by county and week
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Official California state public health agency domain (.ca.gov); data attributed to CDPH Infectious Disease Branch or Vector-Borne Disease Section

iterative_search_queries.query: West Nile virus California August 2024 human cases neuroinvasive deaths county surveillance
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: A broader web search using natural language terms likely to appear in CDPH press releases, county health department reports, and official surveillance summaries. 'Neuroinvasive' is the standard CDC/CDPH classification term for severe WNV disease and will help surface case-classification data. Avoids over-quoted exact phrases that may not match real page text.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH press release, county health department advisory, or westnile.ca.gov summary referencing August 2024 case counts
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: Source attributed to CDPH, a California county public health department, or official state surveillance program

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC ArboNET West Nile virus 2024 California cases deaths statistics

This provides a cross-validation source independent of CDPH and may include August 2024 cumulative figures.

iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: CDC.gov domain; data labeled as ArboNET surveillance system output

likely_reporting_agencies: California Department of Public Health (CDPH) – Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS)
CDC Division of Vector-Borne Diseases (DVBD)
County/Local Health Departments (e.g., Los Angeles County DPH, Sacramento County DPH, Kern County DPH, Fresno County DPH)

validation_source_categories: County-level health department press releases or dashboards
count_semantics_notes: CDPH typically reports cumulative year-to-date human cases; subtract prior period totals if only August 2024 incident counts are needed
ArboNET data may lag by 1–2 weeks from actual reporting date
Neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts should be recorded separately if available, then summed for cases_unspecified if not stratified
Deaths are often underreported in real-time surveillance; cross-check with MMWR annual summaries
Probable cases in WNV context = IgM positive without confirmatory PRNT; confirmed = PRNT or PCR confirmed
disambiguation_risks: WNV surveillance reports often include animal/vector data alongside human data — extract human cases only
Cumulative vs. incident counts: CDPH reports are often cumulative year-to-date; isolate August 2024 period carefully
Confirmed vs. probable: CDPH and ArboNET distinguish confirmed (lab-confirmed) from probable (clinical + epidemiological link); capture both separately
Neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive: case counts are often stratified; aggregate or record separately per schema
'Cases' may refer to mosquito pool positives or dead bird counts in some county reports — verify human case context
County-level reports may use different reporting dates than state-level aggregates — note discrepancies

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Vector-Borne Disease Section (VBDS) publishes weekly WNV human surveillance summaries with county-level confirmed, probable, and suspected case counts, deaths, and hospitalizations. County health departments (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside, San Bernardino, Orange) publish local WNV human case alerts and press releases. These are the highest-priority primary collection sources for the August 2024 California window.

CDC ArboNET publishes structured state-level WNV human case and death data. California open data portals (data.ca.gov) and CDPH open data may expose machine-readable WNV surveillance datasets filterable by county and date, enabling programmatic validation of narrative report extractions.

PAHO and WHO may publish situation reports or epidemiological updates referencing US WNV human case data including California. ProMED-mail archives WNV outbreak alerts that may cite CDPH or CDC data for California August 2024.

Reputable California news outlets (Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and health news aggregators (CIDRAP, Outbreak News Today) may report WNV human case counts citing CDPH or county health department data for August 2024, providing early signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV seasonality, high-risk counties, and case definitions provide context for interpreting August 2024 surveillance data. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific case counts given publication lag, but useful for case definition and count semantics context.
